Affordable Course Materials initiative saves CWU students over $920,000 on textbooks
Central Washington University's Affordable Course Materials initiative has saved students over $920,000 since its launch. The program collaborates with faculty and campus partners to offer low- or no-cost textbooks using open educational resources.
Central Washington University has saved its students an estimated $921,760 on textbooks since launching the Affordable Course Materials initiative, according to an Oct. 7 announcement from the university.
The initiative is overseen by Anna Crosswhite, who became CWU’s first Affordable Course Materials Librarian in 2024. The program works with faculty and the campus bookstore, Wildcat Shop, to identify and provide low- or no-cost course materials for students. “The ACM initiative works with faculty to identify low- or no-cost course materials,” Crosswhite said. “That could be through library-licensed eBooks that are unlimited user access, print course reserves, as well as open educational resources, which are freely available online and can be printed at cost. We also notify them when a textbook they have selected is available through the library.”
Crosswhite said her own experience using Open Educational Resources (OER) during graduate school showed her it was possible to reduce textbook costs significantly for students. She noted that she spent around $40 on textbooks throughout her master’s program due to OER use.
Collaboration between CWU Libraries and Wildcat Shop has been key in tracking inventory data and labeling free books for student access. Dean of Libraries Sydney Thompson said, “Anna has been able to come in and wrangle all of that data and spend a ton of time with textbook lists and communication with faculty.” Wildcat Shop Director Angela Johnson added, “As an independent campus store, we can focus on developing strong partnerships with faculty and the library to expand the adoption of Open Educational Resources and library-licensed content... This independence allows us the flexibility to work on long-term programs that develop innovative, student-centered solutions.”
Faculty engagement is another aspect of the initiative’s approach. Assistant Professor of English Candace Walsh attended a workshop hosted by Crosswhite over the summer focused on redesigning courses for affordability. Walsh said, “I learned how pivotal accessible textbook materials are to first-gen and lower-income families... Anna's presentation and workshop clarified the importance of access to class texts.” Physics Professor Bruce Palmquist praised CWU Libraries’ efforts: “By creating a position like Anna’s, it shows that the library is more than a collection of old books... The library cares about the student experience.”
With ongoing collaboration across departments and continued workshops for faculty interested in reducing costs for their students, Crosswhite says she remains committed to helping both instructors and learners find affordable solutions: “There’s so much of the cost of college that we as educators can’t control,” she said. “But what we can control is what we assign to students and the resource we provide for them.”
